summary: Researched the evening before (Fri 20 Nov); lineups are not out, so this is a draft until the morning check and the final check. Saturday is a full football day (Premier League, Bundesliga, Serie A, La Liga, Ligue 1). Every kept game needs a second price; this time a DraftKings drift of 3% or more against the favourite with no news is treated as low (the warning that came before Troyes slipped on 20 Nov). Eight games were researched; four are medium. Medium: Roma at Parma (Roma unbeaten, 27 pts v 8; DraftKings about 73.5%; Svilar, Mancini and Dybala back), Como v Cagliari (5th v 9th, Cagliari lost three straight; DraftKings about 72%), Man City v Fulham (City have beaten Fulham 20 straight times, but lost three league games in a row and have defensive doubts; DraftKings about 68%), Real Madrid v Celta (eight straight wins, Mbappé fit; DraftKings about 82%; Celta draw a lot). Low: Leverkusen v Paderborn, Monaco v Auxerre and Napoli v Torino (DraftKings drifted 3.5-4% against each favourite with no news), Lazio v Lecce (Gattuso announced rotation and DraftKings drifted). Not researched: PSG at Nice, Leipzig at Union, UFC, tennis. Morning check (Sat 21 Nov): no overnight news hurts the four medium favourites; prices moved slightly toward Man City, Como and Roma and are flat for Real Madrid, with DraftKings in agreement. Parma lose Ndiaye (suspended), Romero and probably Diego Carlos. Lineups are not out, so this is still a draft until the final check. Final check (Sat 21 Nov, about 13:05 UTC): all three slip legs pass. Como's official XI was not out yet; no late news against Como, Roma or Real Madrid, and Polymarket and DraftKings moved toward Como and Roma and are flat for Madrid. AS reports Madrid may rotate before PSV, which if anything helps the Celta +3.5 leg. Per the 20 Nov rule (the final check may only remove legs), only the morning slip's legs are kept as views: the Under 5.5 and Under 4.5 views were dropped so the rebuild cannot swap them in. At the official XI (13:17 UTC) Como benched Nico Paz, so Como was set to low and dropped; the slip shrinks to the two remaining morning legs (no new legs).

checks.team_news: Final check Sat 13:05 UTC. Kick-off is 20:00 UTC, so no official XI is out and ESPN rosters are empty. Latest previews (TribalFootball, Sports Mole, Livescore, Voice of Emirates) are unchanged from this morning. Madrid out: Rodrygo (knee), Asencio (leg), Mendy (hip/thigh). Doubts: Tchouameni (groin) and Bernardo Silva (leg). Vinicius is back from his ban and Mbappe is expected to start. New this afternoon: Livescore, citing AS, says Mourinho will make a number of changes, with Valverde possibly on the bench and Alexander-Arnold at right-back. This is a rotation signal, but unconfirmed and not a key-starter loss. Celta out: Borja Iglesias (calf), Starfelt (hamstring), Roman (knee). The sources disagree on the rest of Celta's doubt list. I found no Saturday press conference news or injury report that changes the picture.
checks.lineups: Not out and will not be before the bet (kick-off 20:00 UTC). Expected Madrid XI in most previews: Courtois; Dumfries, Konate, Huijsen, Cucurella; Valverde, Guler; Diomande, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappe. AS/Livescore: several changes, Alexander-Arnold at right-back, Valverde possibly benched. Celta expected: Radu; Rodriguez, Caceres, Alonso; Rueda, Antanon, Burcio, Carreira; Aspas, Duran, Swedberg, though other previews have Moriba and Jutla in the XI.
checks.rotation: Madrid play PSV in the Champions League midweek. AS reports (via Livescore) that Mourinho is set to make a number of changes. Not confirmed, so a soft rotation risk remains. Madrid have won 8 straight in all competitions.
checks.motivation: Unchanged: Madrid are 2nd with 30 pts, 3 behind Barcelona, and need the points. Celta are 11th with 13 pts. No hard-rule situation.
checks.form: Unchanged: Madrid have 5 league wins in a row and 8 in all competitions; Mbappe has 13 league goals. Celta have 7 draws in 12 league games, no away win this season, and 1 win in their last 5. A draw is the real failure mode, but the slip leg (Celta +3.5) only fails if Madrid win by 4 or more.
checks.h2h: Unchanged: Celta won 2-0 at the Bernabeu in Dec 2025; Madrid won 2-1 at Balaidos in Mar 2026.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket at 13:02 UTC: home 0.8464, draw 0.1073, away 0.0464. First listed was 0.8437 / 0.1028 / 0.0535, so the favourite is +0.3% and has not moved against. The 24h favourite move is flat (0.845 to 0.845). DraftKings via ESPN at 13:01 UTC: Madrid 1.15 (-650), draw +700, Celta +1500 to +1600 (the scoreboard feed gave 16.0, the summary feed +1500). De-vigged 0.822 / 0.119 / 0.059, versus 0.817 / 0.119 / 0.064 this morning, so essentially unchanged and no lengthening. DraftKings total 3.5 (over -110, under -115), spread Madrid -2.5 at -170 for Celta. Polymarket is about 2.4 points above the DraftKings de-vig, inside the band. Slip leg: Polymarket ah_away_+3.5 is 0.765 (unchanged since first listed) and ou_5.5_under is 0.845 (unchanged). DraftKings pricing Madrid -2.5 as the spread and 3.5 goals as the total supports Madrid not winning by 4 or more as a likely outcome.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating (data.rating absent for this club game). Livescore predicts 3-1 and Martin's predicts 3-0 for Madrid, so both fit Celta +3.5. Not independently verified.
checks.venue_weather: Santiago Bernabeu, home game. No weather or pitch problem found.

games.reason: Final check at 13:05 UTC. The XI is not out (kick-off 20:00 UTC), so availability is unconfirmed, which holds confidence at medium. New this afternoon: an AS report via Livescore of several Madrid changes, with Valverde possibly benched, which is soft rotation and cuts against a big Madrid margin if anything. Price is stable (Polymarket +0.3% since first listing, DraftKings de-vig 0.822 vs 0.817 this morning). No hard exclusion applies. The Celta +3.5 and Under 5.5 legs are backed by the market, with views set at or just below it.
games.main_risk: A heavy Madrid win by 4 or more goals (Mbappe, Vinicius and Bellingham in an attack against a Celta side missing Iglesias, Starfelt and Roman), which would sink the Celta +3.5 leg. Market and DraftKings put that at roughly 1 in 4. For the match result, a draw or 1-0 / 1-1 is still the failure mode, and Madrid rotation ahead of PSV is unconfirmed.

checks.team_news: Leverkusen: Rotowire (Fri) says coach Martinez confirmed Kofane (thigh) and Diaby (thigh) available, Kofane possibly as sub first. Bulinews/Yahoo: Tella also expected back, Doue close but behind; Maza (ankle picked up on Algeria duty) doubtful, club hopes he is fit. Sports Mole lists Tella, Terrier and Kofane as out, so sources conflict. Paderborn: only Gayret (knee, out to January) per Sports Mole. No Kettemann press-conference injury list found. Coach Martinez (appointed June 2026) says Paderborn are well prepared and Leverkusen must be strong at the back; Kettemann says it is a demanding away game with focus on defending. Maza's fitness and which internationals returned late are not confirmed.
checks.lineups: Predicted (not official; lineups come out ~60 min before kickoff). Bundesliga.com 4-2-3-1: Flekken; Gutierrez, Medina, Tapsoba, Quansah; Aleix Garcia, E. Fernandez; Moreira, Maza, Diaby; Schick. Sports Mole: same names (Diaby, Maza, Moreira behind Schick). Paderborn 3-3-2-2/3-5-2: Noll; Hansen, Scheller, ter Horst; Curda, Baack, Castaneda, Obermair, Vidovic; Pieringer, Marino. Both outlets agree on the core, Maza is the open question.
checks.rotation: No European or cup game in the window; the match follows the international break. Leverkusen last played the 2-1 win at Koln (Schick's 8th league goal), before that a 4-2 home loss to Stuttgart and a 3-0 loss at Hoffenheim. No rotation signal; Paderborn run about 122 km per game, 2nd highest in the league.
checks.motivation: Table before the game: Leverkusen 5th, 16 pts from 9 (5W 1D 3L, 20:17), 5 points behind Bayern/Dortmund; Paderborn 13th, 10 pts (2W 4D 3L, 8:11), 3 points above the play-off place, so both sides need the points. Not a derby; the favourite has not secured anything, so no hard exclusion. Head coaches: Martinez since June, Kettemann long in post (no change in the last 7 days).
checks.form: Leverkusen league last six W W W L L W; leaky at home lately (4-2 vs Stuttgart, 3-0 at Hoffenheim, 17 goals conceded in 9 games), but won their first five home games. Paderborn W L D W D D, unbeaten in 4 (club record equalled in the Bundesliga), only one away loss all season, 11 conceded in 9 (best start of their top-flight history) but only 8 scored in 9, 2-2 draw with Frankfurt last time. Sources: Bundesliga.com, beIN Sports, Sports Mole. No xG found.
checks.h2h: Leverkusen have never lost to Paderborn in 7 meetings (6W 1D), including a 3-1 DFB-Pokal win at the BayArena (Bulinews listing). Paderborn are a deep, compact, high-running side with little scoring; the likely path to a Leverkusen non-win is a low-scoring 0-0/1-1.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/ger.1/scoreboard?dates=20261121): home 1.26, draw 6.0, away 8.0, total 3.5, de-vigged home 0.732, draw 0.153, away 0.115. The opening line was home 1.21, draw 6.5, away 8.0, so the home price has drifted out (implied about 0.826 to 0.794 raw, a fall of about 4% relative). Polymarket over the same period: 0.765 to 0.775 over 24h (+1.3%), so the two sources move in opposite directions and I found no news explaining the DK drift; Kofane/Diaby/Tella return news is positive for Leverkusen, Maza doubt is the only negative. Polymarket volume about $10.9k on the event (home market about $2.3k), liquidity about $305k, so the market is thin. DK de-vigged home is 4 points below Polymarket, hence my p.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating retrieved (ClubElo returned nothing and candidate data has no rating for club games). Sports Mole's model page gives 58.7% / 22.97% / 18.29% and predicts 2-0 (method unknown, lower than the market). I treat this as a gap and shade the home price down 3-4 points.
checks.venue_weather: BayArena, Leverkusen, normal home venue, Sat 21 Nov 14:30 UTC. No weather or pitch problem found, but I did not locate a specific forecast.

games.reason: Verified Bundesliga matchday 10, Leverkusen at home against a mid-table side, no hard exclusion. The favourite's price is supported by the return of Diaby and Kofane, but Leverkusen's defence is leaky, Maza is doubtful, and Paderborn are in record form with the best defensive start of their top-flight history. DraftKings is 4 points below Polymarket on the home win and no rating model was retrieved, so I shade p below the market and rate it medium. Set to low at review: DraftKings lengthened Leverkusen from 1.21 to 1.26 (about 4% against the favourite) with no news found to explain it, the same warning sign that preceded Troyes slipping on 20 Nov; the morning check can restore medium only if the move is explained or reversed.
games.main_risk: A draw (0-0 or 1-1): Paderborn defend deep, concede little, run a lot and are unbeaten in 4, while Leverkusen have conceded 17 in 9 and lost 2 of the last 3 league games; Maza's ankle and returning players' match fitness are unconfirmed, and DraftKings drifted from 1.21 to 1.26 without a clear explanation.

checks.team_news: Checked again at 13:05 UTC: no new news hurting Roma. The morning reading holds: Svilar, Mancini and Dybala back (Gasperini: striker and keeper recovered and will start from minute 1), Pellegrini and Rensch out. New this afternoon: one report says Svilar's selection is only confirmed in the hours before kick-off, with Gollini as backup (small doubt). Parma are still without Ndiaye (suspended) and Romero (out), with Diego Carlos and Drobnic doubtful; Bernabe is fine. Nothing worse for Parma and nothing worse for Roma.
checks.lineups: Official XIs are NOT out (ESPN rosters empty at 13:05 UTC; kick-off 17:00 UTC, so XIs come around 15:45-16:00). Latest expected Roma 3-4-2-1: Svilar; Mancini, N'Dicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Dybala behind Malen, Mora or Soule in the other slot (previews split, Siamo la Roma has a Mora-Dybala-Malen attack). Expected Parma 3-5-2: Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Carboni; midfield and attack names differ by source. Unconfirmed.
checks.rotation: Roma play PSG in the Champions League on Wednesday 25 Nov, still a soft risk. Nothing today points to heavy rotation: Dybala and Svilar are expected back in the XI. Roma are rested after the break.
checks.motivation: Unchanged: Roma 27 pts from 11 (8W 3D 0L), chasing the top; Parma 16th on 8 pts in the relegation fight. No hard rule hit.
checks.form: Roma last five W D W W W, unbeaten; Parma last five L L D W L with only 9 goals in 11 games. Gasperini calls it a 'partita trappola'.
checks.h2h: Last meeting Parma 2-3 Roma on 10 May 2026 (single source). Roma score about 2.8 per game, Parma about 0.8.
checks.odds: Polymarket live 13:02 UTC: Parma 0.0664, draw 0.1371, Roma 0.7964. First listing 0.0835 / 0.1529 / 0.7635, so Roma are up 3.3 points (+4.3%) since first listed, toward the favourite, and the move is explained by the Parma absences and Roma's returns. Roma were 0.7836 this morning, now 0.7964, still rising. DraftKings via ESPN this afternoon: Parma 10.5, draw 6.0, Roma 1.22 (this morning +900/+500/-425), de-vigged 0.088 / 0.154 / 0.758, moved slightly toward Roma. DraftKings is about 4 points below Polymarket on Roma, which agrees within 5 points but is a gap to respect. Polymarket legs: Parma +3.5 0.805 (0.835 at first listing, down 3 points, so Roma are expected to win bigger), Under 4.5 0.735 (0.765 at first listing). DraftKings total line 3.5, Roma -1.5 around -150. Polymarket volume is thin.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free rating available (no rating in the candidates data, ClubElo unreachable). Substitute is the season record: Roma goal difference +21 in 11 games vs Parma -8, 27 pts vs 8. Not an Elo or Opta model.
checks.venue_weather: Stadio Ennio Tardini, Parma, normal home venue, 18:00 local (17:00 UTC). No weather or pitch problem found. Parma's coach Gilardino has been in post since 29 Sep 2026, so no hard coach rule applies.

games.reason: Roma are 27 pts from 11 unbeaten against a Parma side with 8 pts and 9 goals scored, and Parma are missing Ndiaye and Romero. The Parma +3.5 leg (Roma do not win by 4 or more) still looks safe: Roma win by 4+ only in a rare heavy win, and Parma's low scoring, a 3.5 DraftKings total and a 0.735 Under 4.5 price all support it. Prices moved toward Roma, but the Parma +3.5 price fell from 0.835 to 0.805 because a bigger Roma win is now somewhat likelier. Confidence is medium because the XIs are not official and the Svilar and Mora/Soule slots are open. I back the leg slightly below the market.
games.main_risk: A big Roma win of 4 or more goals: Roma average 2.8 goals per game, the market has shifted toward a bigger Roma margin since first listing (+3.5 down from 0.835 to 0.805), and the draw/upset risk is irrelevant to this leg. Lineups are unconfirmed. Roma's Champions League game vs PSG on Wednesday is a soft rotation risk, which would help this leg.

checks.team_news: Afternoon re-check (13:02-13:08 UTC): the official XIs are NOT out yet; the ESPN summary rosters were empty and web search found only predicted lineups. Morning findings still hold: Como without Kean (out for months) and Diao, Jesus Rodriguez and Addai out; Chalobah unlikely to start; Nico Paz expected to start. Cagliari: Obert, Nzola, Trepy and Fadera recovered, Winks and Mina out. New this afternoon: Adnkronos (today) predicts Como 4-2-3-1 Butez; Couto, Ramon, Kempf, Valle; Da Cunha, Perrone; Caqueret, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas, and Cagliari 4-4-2 Caprile; Ze Pedro, Kofler, Rodriguez, Obert; Adopo, Deiola, Romano, Fazzini; Maldini, Mendy. It reports no late injuries or changes, but it is a probable XI only. No new negative news found. Official XI (13:17 UTC): Nico Paz, Como's key creative player, is benched, so Como start without Kean, Diao and Paz.
checks.lineups: OFFICIAL XIs (ESPN, 13:17 UTC). Como 4-2-3-1: Butez; Couto, Ramon, Kempf, Kaiki; Milla, Ricci; Liberali, Da Cunha, Baturina; Douvikas. Nico Paz is on the BENCH (expected to start in every preview; he returned late from Argentina), with Perrone, Chalobah and Valle also on the bench. Cagliari 4-2-3-1: Caprile; Ze Pedro, Kofler, Deiola, Obert; Adopo, Romano; Grandu, Fazzini, Maldini; Mendy.
checks.rotation: No rotation concern: neither side has a midweek game. The only issue remains the late return of the Argentina players, with Paz still predicted to start.
checks.motivation: Unchanged: Como 5th chasing the top four, Cagliari 9th and mid-table on a three-game losing run, with no hard-rule situation.
checks.form: Unchanged: Como W 3-1 at Torino, W 2-0 Sassuolo, W 3-1 at Fiorentina, 0-0 Roma, L 0-2 Frosinone, W 2-1 Parma. Cagliari have lost three straight and conceded 10 in them.
checks.h2h: Como won 2-1 at Cagliari in March 2026. Older head-to-head data is undated, so I do not rely on it.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket Como 0.7635 (draw 0.1529, Cagliari 0.0835), up 0.9% from 0.7565 at first listing (+0.7 points); the 24h move was 0.755 to 0.765. DraftKings via ESPN at 13:01 UTC: Como 1.26 (-380), draw 5.50, Cagliari 9.00, de-vigged 73.0/16.8/10.2, total 3.5. Since this morning (1.28/5.50/8.50, 72.3/16.8/10.9) the Como price has shortened slightly, so nothing has moved against the favourite and the two sources agree on direction. The book is about 3 points below Polymarket, within the 5-point band. My p of 0.73 matches the de-vigged book and sits under the market. At the XI (13:17 UTC): Polymarket Como 0.755 Yes (about 0.76 normalised, flat), DraftKings -360 (from -380 at 13:01), a slight lengthening.
checks.models: No ClubElo or Opta rating was read. The table gap (Como 5th, +8 goal difference, against Cagliari 9th, -5) and the DraftKings price are the only rating evidence, so this check is weak.
checks.venue_weather: Stadio Sinigaglia, Como, Saturday 21 Nov, 15:00 local (14:00 UTC). A normal home game; no pitch or weather problem found, though no forecast was read.

games.reason: Rated low at the official XI: Nico Paz, Como's key creative player and expected starter, is on the bench, and Kean and Diao are out. Under the final-check rule a key starter missing makes the game low, so the leg is dropped. The price has barely moved (Polymarket about 0.76, DraftKings -380 to -360).
games.main_risk: Como start without Nico Paz (benched), Kean and Diao, so the attack is thin; a draw or a narrow loss is the way the favourite fails.

checks.team_news: Lazio out: Nuno Tavares, Marusic (minor setback), Sutalo (all in rehab; Gattuso reassesses next week) and Zaccagni (swelling, decision next week). Frattesi is back from the international break with a minor knock, trained all week and is available. Gudmundsson (shoulder) and Rovella available; Cataldi missed one session, nothing serious. The Danish internationals returned the day after their match. No suspensions or yellow-card risks for either side (Lazionews 20 Nov 21:14, Sky Sport and Il Messaggero Gattuso press conference of 20 Nov). Lecce: Ilic and Pierotti out; Monteiro and Berisha back from individual training and called up (26 called up); Camarda to be assessed on the day (Tuttosport, Lazionews, Calcio Lecce 20 Nov).
checks.lineups: Expected XIs are not confirmed. Lazionews (20 Nov) has Lazio 4-3-3: Mandas; Floriani Mussolini, Leite, Provstgaard, Pedraza; Dele-Bashiru, Belahyane, Taylor; Isaksen, Pinamonti, Noslin. Fantamaster (18 Nov) has Doekhi in for Provstgaard and Frattesi in midfield. The defence and midfield differ by source and Gattuso named no XI. Lecce: 4-3-3 with Falcone; Veiga, Gaspar, Gabriel, Gallo; Coulibaly, Ngom, Maleh; N'Dri, Stulic, Fatah (Lazionews), or 3-5-1-1 with Geubbels and Fatah (Fantamaster). Di Francesco said Monteiro can start.
checks.rotation: Lazio's last game before the break was 1-1 at Napoli on 8 Nov. They went out of the Coppa Italia to Mantova (Lazio Family results 14-18 Nov), so there is no midweek game. The main soft risk is Gattuso's own words: several players who have had little game time will start from the first minute, and he said he will have to rotate (Laziostory, Gold TV 20 Nov). Frattesi and the Danish internationals came back from the break. A derby is next but has no confirmed date in my sources, and Gattuso said it is not on his mind. Lecce took 7 of 10 points away from home and have no stated rotation.
checks.motivation: Lazio are first in Serie A with 29 points, one ahead of Inter and two ahead of Roma (365scores). They are unbeaten and want a win to hold first place. Lecce are 14th with 10 points and need points to stay clear of the bottom. Both sides have something to play for, so no hard exclusion applies.
checks.form: Lazio: 9W 2D 0L, unbeaten (365scores). Recent results: 2-1 v Cagliari (1 Nov), 1-1 at Napoli (8 Nov) after six straight league wins. They have the league's best defence with 9 conceded in 11. Away from home they scored 12 and conceded 3 in their last 4, but at home 9 scored and 5 conceded in their last 4. They have 11 first-half goals in their last 8. Lecce: 3W 1D 7L, recent form D-L-L-L-W, 12 scored and 22 conceded in 11. The Coppa Italia loss to Mantova shows Lazio can slip when they rotate. I found no xG data.
checks.h2h: I did not find recent h2h results in the sources I read, so I am not relying on it. Sarri's older Lazio-Lecce results (2023-24) are not informative with new coaches on both sides. Lecce are well drilled and dangerous on set pieces (Gattuso).
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (https://site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/soccer/ita.1/scoreboard?dates=20261121): Lazio 1.38, draw 4.70, Lecce 7.00, de-vigged 0.671 / 0.197 / 0.132. The line opened at 1.32 and has drifted out to 1.38, which is a small move away from Lazio. Polymarket 0.704 / 0.183 / 0.114 sits about 3 points above the de-vigged DraftKings price on the favourite. Other Italian books quote Lazio around 1.35-1.40, draw 4.80, Lecce 6.75, over 2.5 at 1.55-1.63 and both teams to score 1.82-1.90 (Spaziocalcio, Agimeg, WebPronostici snippets). The DraftKings total is 2.5. Polymarket 24h move: 0.705 to 0.705, flat. Polymarket event volume is about 42.6k (Lazio win market about 31.6k, Lecce win about 10.8k, draw market about 0.16k), so the draw price is thin.
checks.models: No ClubElo or other bookmaker-free rating was retrievable tonight (the ClubElo API returned nothing, and candidates data.rating is absent for clubs). The proxy is the table and goals record: Lazio 1st with the best defence (0.82 goals conceded per game against a 1.55 league average), Lecce 14th conceding 2.0 per game.
checks.venue_weather: Stadio Olimpico, Rome, Saturday 21 Nov, 15:00 local (14:00 UTC), live on DAZN, referee Marcenaro. This is Lazio's normal home ground with no unusual venue. I found no reports of weather or pitch problems, but I did not check a forecast.

games.reason: Lazio are the clear table-topper and the best defence against a weak 14th-placed side, and the market is in line with DraftKings at 0.67 to 0.70. I lowered the home win p to 0.665, near the DraftKings de-vig, because of the stated rotation (Gattuso: those who played little will start), the Frattesi/Zaccagni/Danes post-break doubts, and Lazio's 9 goals conceded at home in recent games being less tight than away. No hard rule applies: Gattuso is not new, the fixture is not a derby, the venue is normal, and neither side has nothing left to play for. Confidence is medium because there is no bookmaker-free rating and the XI is not confirmed. Set to low at review: Gattuso said several players with little game time will start (rotation announced by the coach), and DraftKings lengthened Lazio from 1.32 to 1.38 (about 4% against the favourite). News that hurts the favourite plus a price move against it is a low under the rules.
games.main_risk: A draw or a narrow 1-0 or 1-1 result against a well-organised Lecce, which is dangerous on set pieces, while Lazio rotate several fringe players (Gattuso said so) after the break and the 0-0 or 1-1 home draw-type games. Their Coppa Italia loss to Mantova shows the cost of rotating.

checks.team_news: Morning update (21 Nov). Sports Mole (Maresca press conference report): Maresca confirmed two City doubts and gave a Guehi update; Guehi is reported to start, the hip problem was a 'small issue' at Forest and not a reason for rest. Other previews are less sure (one says fitness unclear, one still calls him a major doubt), so this is not confirmed. Gvardiol is expected to be available (played the full game for Croatia on 12 Nov despite going off at half-time against Forest); one preview has him moving to centre-back if Guehi is out. Still out: Semenyo (knee). Doubtful: Nunes and Khusanov. Fulham news is unchanged from last night: Smith Rowe and Lecomte out, Cairney doubtful. No new City absence found since Friday. I read only search summaries this morning, not the full press-conference text.
checks.lineups: Predicted City XIs this morning still differ at full-back and wide: Donnarumma; Lewis or Nunes, Dias, Guehi or Gvardiol, O'Reilly; Anderson, Fernandez (or Bouaddi); Doku, Cherki, Foden or Ndiaye; Haaland. Fulham as last night (Leno; Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Garcia or Muniz). Official lineups not out; to be checked at the final check.
checks.rotation: No change. City have had a full week since the break and no midweek game. No rotation signal for either side. Official lineups will show this.
checks.motivation: No change from last night. City need points after three straight league losses. No hard-rule situation for either side. League table gap still not checked.
checks.form: No change. City lost three straight league games (last one 3-1 at Forest); Fulham are unbeaten in four league games (2W 2D). Neither has a coach change inside the rule window. xG not found.
checks.h2h: No change. Fulham are chasing an end to a record 20-game losing run against City; the latest meeting I could confirm was a 3-0 City win in Feb 2026. One preview notes Bassey eyeing a 22-year record.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket: City 0.7165, draw 0.1669, Fulham 0.1166. Last night (and first listing): 0.7035 / 0.1731 / 0.1234.
